correctness.rationale: Two-step slow-variable increments force x1+x2=2sigma; elimination is reversible for u!=0 and yields exactly one positive quadratic root per prime-two orbit. The quadratic is monotone for 0<sigma<=1 and has a unique positive minimum for sigma>1, proving the exhaustive boundary counts. The exact two-step Jacobian identities were symbolically reconstructed. At sigma=2, alpha=5, eta=1/1000, the radical bound 1.997<sqrt(7984/2001)<1.998 and explicit Schur inequalities certify fixed-point and large-q two-cycle sinks and the small-q saddle. No finite experiment is used for exhaustive counting.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the lowest nontrivial periodic orbits of a standard fast–slow neuronal map over an unbounded three-parameter real domain. It identifies a finite-amplitude two-cycle fold before the fixed-point flip in sigma>1, including exact degeneracy boundaries, and certifies coexistence of a fixed sink, period-two sink and period-two saddle at a source-studied parameter. Unlike attractor plots, the exact census locates an unstable candidate basin separator. No assertion of global basins or longer periods is needed for this value.
